readability.evidence: Names and PHPDoc are clear (Ticket.php:245-268, Queue.php:153-189), but nested try/catch branches in TicketFactory.php:402-422 and Ticket.php:341-355 are hard to follow and largely dead (issued_at is always set by definition), and the overloaded nextCode signature obscures intent.

scope.evidence: All edits (IssueTicket, UpdateQueue, Queue, Ticket, TicketFactory, two migrations, business-rules, database-schema, CHANGELOG) serve the task; no unrelated refactors or UI.

issues.explanation: A large feature (prefix map validation, daily per-prefix sequence, migration, UpdateQueue parameter, factory behaviour) ships with zero tests, violating the project's mandatory TDD convention.
Codes switch from 'A001' to 'N001' but no existing tests are updated, so any test asserting the old A-sequence will fail and the suite is likely red.
nextCode accepts prefix-or-priority (including numeric strings) with a hidden queue lookup that no caller uses; a plain string prefix parameter suffices.
issue_date derivation is duplicated with defensive try/catch(\Throwable) and dead branches instead of a single small helper.
down() restores unique(queue_id, code), which will fail once daily-restarted codes (e.g. N001 on two days) exist, so the rollback is not reliably reversible.
Backfill iterates rows in PHP with per-row updates rather than a single DATE(issued_at) update as the task describes.
Migration timestamps (000001/000002) suggest hand-written files rather than make:migration output.

review.summary: The change implements priority-letter prefixes with a validated per-queue override, a daily per-prefix sequence keyed on a new issue_date column, single-clock issuance, UpdateQueue support and documentation updates, and the logic appears correct and secure. However, it ships with no tests at all and does not update existing tests that depend on A-codes, violating the project's mandatory TDD convention, and it adds speculative/duplicated defensive code; it needs substantial work before approval.
